messages:
Alicia: FYI I received Azure's EDP draft — notable items: 1) a region-minimum, 2) spot-fallback clause, 3) billing defined as "GPU-month" = 720 GPU-hours per full GPU.

Mike: paste the exact wording for the fallback & SLA please.

Bob_Azure: Pasting excerpt from their legal template:

Bob_Azure: "Customer commits to a 12-month GPU EDP of 1,200 GPU-months across supported regions. Provider will guarantee 90% capacity within agreed regions during standard hours. Spot-fallback is permitted for up to 10% of committed units with preemption notice. Missed capacity >5% entitles customer to service credits equal to 1% of monthly commitment per percentage point."

Sourav: 1,200 GPU-months is ok as a headline but we need a region split (e.g., eastus / westeurope). Also what are 'standard hours'?

Bob_Azure: Their legal defines "standard hours" = Mon-Fri 06:00-22:00 local region time. They will price 24x7 guarantees at a higher discount threshold.

Jess: We need 24x7 in our primary regions. Most production latency-sensitive routes are global. Also clarify GPU-month granularity — is it per whole GPU or vGPU?

Alicia: Their draft bills per full GPU (720h blocks). No vGPU fractional billing — that will cause waste for dev/smaller clusters.

Mike: That's big. We should ask for vGPU or fractional crediting, or at least a conversion table across SKUs.

Sourav: Suggest negotiating a conversion table: e.g., 1x A100-80GB = 4x A100-20GB equivalents for credit accounting.

Bob_Azure: They said metering complexity is the reason for whole-GPU only. Will consider a conversion table if we provide expected SKU mapping.

Alicia: Spot-fallback up to 10% is acceptable only if provider gives 30min preemption notice for committed units or automatic failover to our Dedicated pool/other region at committed rates.

Sourav: 5 minutes is useless for draining KV caches and checkpointing. We need 30 minutes for critical SKUs, maybe 15min for non-critical.

Bob_Azure: They offered 15 minutes for committed instances. I'll push; 30 minutes may reduce the discount.

Jess: Overage rate in template is 2.1x on-demand. We should cap overage at 1.5x or allow spare capacity to be billed at committed rates once baseline exceeded.

Mike: Also push for stronger missed-capacity credits. 1% per percent beyond 5% is tiny. Propose either higher credits or right to draw from provider spot pool at committed pricing during shortages.

Alicia: Proposed negotiation asks (first pass):
- Region-level minimums with roll-up flexibility (60% primary regions, 40% portable)
- Fractional GPU-month accounting or conversion table
- 24x7 guarantee in primary regions with 15-30min preemption notice on committed units
- Overage capped at 1.5x or automatic move to committed tier
- Ramp schedule (6 months to full commit) with pro-rata true-ups
- Invoice breakout by region+SKU and tagging requirements in SOW

Sourav: Add requirement for a per-region capacity dashboard (7-day rolling availability) and 30-day proactive shortage alerts.

Mike: Finance insists on audit rights and line-item invoices for chargebacks. No blended opaque billing.

Jess: Legal wants the SOW to include all these operational SLAs — don't leave them only in the master EDP.

Bob_Azure: I'll draft a redline and propose: conversion table + 15min preemption + 6-month ramp as initial asks. Will push region dashboard + invoice format as hard requirements.

Sourav: Fine to start there, but mark preemption negotiable up to 30min for critical SKUs.

Alicia: And add a clause: if they miss >10% of the commit for two consecutive months, we can pause payments for affected months until remediation or take additional credits.

Mike: Procurement/Finance okay to trade some list discount for better SLA credits and transparency.

Jess: Early termination fee in draft is 60% of remaining commitment — ask to reduce to a 30% sliding scale if we provide migration notice and an acceptable transition plan.

Bob_Azure: They'll likely prefer fixed penalties but open to sliding scale with defined migration windows.

procurement-bot: Contract draft uploaded: https://internal/contracts/EDP-AZ-17855-draft.pdf

Alicia: Scheduling a quick sync 9am PT tomorrow to triage the redline before we reply. Please review when Bob posts it.

Mike: I'll review redline for finance impact. Thanks all.
